messages:
morgan: Quick summary from the networking spike — we have two viable patterns for private control plane egress from customer VPCs: (A) attach customer accounts to a shared Transit Gateway and rely on centralized route propagation, or (B) publish per-customer Interface Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) + NAT/egress proxies in each account. Need a decision for the CP separation RFC follow-up.

rafa: nice, can you call out the top tradeoffs?

morgan: sure — high level: TGW = single routing plane, easier to reason about pathing (single place to update policies), fewer per-customer resources to manage. Cons: cross-account attachment lifecycle, route table size & convergence concerns, harder to enforce per-tenant egress quotas, and blast radius when a route flaps.

carmen: endpoints + NAT gives stronger per-account isolation and easier billing, right? each customer keeps their own egress and we only maintain endpoint services in CP account.

morgan: correct. Endpoints push more operational overhead — we need per-account endpoint service discovery, VPC endpoint limits, and per-customer NAT or proxy fleet (cost + patch surface). But failover is more isolated.

katie: what about latency and SLO? TGW hop could be slightly faster since no extra NAT, but if TGW route tables are large we might see convergence jitter during updates. Any data from the spike?

morgan: microbenchmarks: control RPC p95 to hosted CP via TGW ~12ms, via PrivateLink+proxy ~18ms (proxy adds ~6ms median). Under route churn TGW had some transient 50-200ms spikes in 5% of synthetic sessions when we toggled many attachments.

ivy: that convergence noise worries me. Can we mitigate with staged rollouts and pinned routes per-tenant?

morgan: possible approaches: 1) sharded TGW route tables (per-region/segment) to limit propagation blast radius, 2) limit attachment churn by batching onboarding windows, 3) maintain a read-only per-tenant fallback via endpoint if TGW detects instability. Each adds complexity.

rafa: Sharded TGW seems attractive but how many shards? and what's the operational cost?

morgan: spike notes: 8 shards per-region reduces per-table entries to <10k in our synthetic scale and brought convergence spikes down. Ops cost: add an attachment mapping service and a small controller to pick shards during onboarding.

carmen: Are there AWS quota surprises — max attachments, routes, etc? Need to document for sales/solutions.

morgan: yes — two things to call out: TGW route table entries and attachment limits (varies by account/region), and endpoint service quotas per endpoint-service consumer. We'll surface explicit limits in the RFC.

katie: Security/least-privilege: with TGW the CP has more lateral visibility into customer VPCs unless we enforce strict subnet/scoping. Endpoints + NAT gives clearer boundary (customer owns their egress). Which is better for regulated customers?

morgan: endpoints win for compliance-heavy customers. TGW can be made safe, but it's more work and more review.

ivy: For cost modeling — TGW centralizes egress bandwidth and may be cheaper at scale vs hundreds of small NATs, but cross-account data transfer pricing and attachment fees matter. Do we have model numbers?

morgan: preliminary model attached in spike doc (I posted link in the repo), but ballpark: small customers favor endpoint+NAT (lower constant cost), mid/large customers can be cheaper on TGW due to shared egress. We'll add a unit-economics table in RFC.

rafa: operational playbooks — what about incident scenarios? for TGW, route-table corruption or a bad controller bug could impact many customers. For endpoints, a bad proxy rollout hits one customer at a time. Which risk profile do we prefer?

morgan: tradeoff: TGW is lower ops footprint but higher blast radius. Endpoints increase ops work but reduce systemic risk.

carmen: any hybrid options? like TGW for low-risk customers, endpoints for high-risk/regulatory ones?

morgan: yes — recommended default: start with TGW for self-serve/onboarded customers under a size threshold, require endpoint+dedicated egress for enterprise/regulatory customers. Hybrid routing and fallback semantics: we can offer a per-tenant flag to opt into PrivateLink mode.

katie: Implementation checklist request for RFC: list of TODOs we need to land this.

morgan: noted — will include: 1) TGW shard controller spec, 2) attachment lifecycle API and safe-batch onboarding, 3) endpoint service automation for PrivateLink, 4) per-tenant cost estimator, 5) monitoring: route convergence dashboards + per-tenant egress SLOs, 6) incident playbooks for TGW route corruption and endpoint proxy rollbacks.

infra-bot: deploy:controlplane-tgw-controller v0.1.0 promoted to staging — checks passed :rocket:

ivy: thanks all. My take: start with TGW + shards, ship the controller and monitoring, and keep PrivateLink automation as the enterprise path. We should flag the compliance tradeoffs prominently in the RFC.

morgan: agreed — I'll draft the follow-up RFC with the decision, the shard-controller design, and a clear opt-in path to PrivateLink. Will ping for reviews once draft is up.

rafa: +1 to the hybrid approach. Please include the cost model and short incident runbooks.

carmen: +1. Also add a migration plan for customers on older peering patterns.

morgan: Will do — thanks everyone.
